scope: Managed Fara installation, default MCP-first HostSession startup, controlled login handback and failed real GitHub task qualification
productionChanges: Optional HostSession browser factory allows explicit actual WebKit opt-in tests while default XCTest external-service/browser guards remain intact.

Optional Fara request/response body observer is nil in normal runtime composition. Only the explicit public-site diagnostic supplies a recorder. Bodies exclude transport authentication headers; the test omits screenshots.
findings: The actual installer reused two SHA-verified cached Fara artifacts in its locked staging directory, then verified/promoted the package and wrote its own installation/activation records. This is not a fresh network-download test.
Real runtime validation loaded the managed Fara model and projector, shut down and joined its worker, and left the native-text receipt unchanged.

With Fara installed, default HostSession still reaches the exact MCP draft approval with no model worker. The final 8.85-second run samples zero workers 63 times and sends no approval, so no Mail action executes.

The host control entry point and phone-envelope entry point both reject Resume while the controlled sign-in popup remains open. Closing the popup alone does not resume. Explicit later Resume continues the retained exact goal, once, against fresh state without replanning.
GitHub attempt01 failed in the XCTest browser-creation guard. Explicit browser injection fixes the harness; no global guard was weakened.
GitHub attempt02 reaches the correct release page but returns invalidResponse after 98.87 seconds. It has no raw model-exchange trace, so the precise rejecting stage remains undetermined.
Attempt03 failed compilation at the diagnostic callback expression; an explicit callback type fixed it before inference.

Attempt04 records ten valid decoded actor responses, including navigation, pointer actions, scrolling and Find. The model searches for an exact publication date without completing or calling its page-reading capability. The 100-second task deadline ends the diagnostic; shutdown completes at 106.06 seconds with no worker left. This does not reproduce or explain attempt02 invalidResponse.

Both executed public workflows use at most one sampled worker, retain the oracle outside model input, perform no approved consequential effect and fail the unchanged whole-answer oracle. No browser-task acceptance is claimed.
limitations: 33 distinct current-build methods pass (32 focused, one actual managed startup); the earlier real installation test is separate evidence. This is not a full-suite or release pass.
The popup test uses actual owned WebKit and a controlled local provider; real account/provider authentication and physical-phone/rendered-client testing remain open.
The normal installed /Applications app was not replaced. Actual test-host composition uses an isolated ledger/channel and an explicit owned-browser factory because XCTest suppresses implicit UI.
GitHub attempt04 additionally injects the normal runtime/loader with a diagnostic observer and isolated Fara journal; it is not identical to the default-composition attempt02.
No conclusion is established about missing time metadata: CUA showed a blank release-time caption, but the model did not request a page read and page metadata was not independently tested.
UI-responsiveness warnings remain in the regression and startup bundles. Attempt02 also has negative width/height geometry warnings.
Whole-Mac 12 GB memory, heat, idle residency and general task/model accuracy remain unqualified. Fara browser selection and the production 4 GiB worker cap are unchanged.
sourceScope: The final runtime/test source was compiled in managed-github-release-04 and reused without edits in both final qualifying bundles. Earlier runs retain their separate outcomes and commands.

cacheSeed.scope: Verified cached model data cloned into actual installer staging under the normal installation lock; no receipt or activation record written
